name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Cheap large drug maker with earnings momentum and a strong price trend; acts as a defensive anchor during the move out of tech.
targets.risks: Keytruda's patent expiry and drug-pricing policy.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Leading US steelmaker benefiting from tariff-protected pricing and steady infrastructure demand; the stock is near its 52-week high.
targets.risks: Steel prices falling back if demand softens.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Pipeline and processing business tied to Permian gas volumes, with fee-based cash flow and buybacks.
targets.risks: Lower Permian drilling activity or weak commodity-linked margins.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Top cybersecurity platform with long-term growth; the $495M acquisitions add AI security features.
targets.risks: Very high valuation in a market that is selling tech.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Q3 adjusted EPS of $26.93 beat estimates, the dividend rose 10%, and MPLX cash flow plus buybacks support the stock.
targets.risks: Refiner margins falling back from peak levels.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: Its slimmed-down specialty-materials business is earning more money and the stock trend is strong.
targets.risks: Industrial demand slowing, plus PFAS legal costs.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: Cheap generic-drug maker that is repricing upward on debt reduction, cash returns to shareholders and new pipeline drugs.
targets.risks: Generic price erosion and setbacks at manufacturing plants.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Storage company gaining from AI data infrastructure, with high margins and a reasonable valuation.
targets.risks: The AI hardware selloff keeps squeezing its valuation.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Most efficient large refiner, with heavy cash returns to shareholders.
targets.risks: Same refiner-margin risk as MPC, which concentrates the energy exposure.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth management brings steady fees, and investment banking is recovering.
targets.risks: Weak markets hurting trading and dealmaking revenue.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Revenue grew 20% and billings 29%, guidance went up, and the stock already reflects the bad news.
targets.risks: Stock is volatile and below its 200-day average, so it could keep falling with the sector.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Raised its full-year revenue forecast to $4.64-4.66B and its EPS forecast to $5.40-5.45; free cash flow is up sharply despite the revenue miss.
targets.risks: Slow growth and research-funding pressure keep the stock from being rerated.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Test-equipment maker benefiting from AI and 6G spending; the latest reported quarter showed 36% revenue growth and the selloff appears to be sector-wide, not company-specific.
targets.risks: Stock is below its 200-day average, and the mid-to-late November earnings report could disappoint.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
